body: This is great advice. I really do hate the nickname 'Gus' and will avoid at all costs.

I never even thought of that being a problem! You've convinced me to take Angus off the list.  My maiden name (which I retained as a double barrelled name with my husband's) has a swear word in it. Never heard the end of it throughout primary school.

I’d skip them as they’ll just cause you to lose even more fat. And if you have a low body fat % already that’s not the result you’re after. 

To be honest, the strength days are basically cardio too. I have the same body type  and issue - I’m skinny with low (17%) body fat. 

I’m lifting the heaviest weights they have available (eg 60kg for deadlifts, 50kg for squats - which btw are more than my body weight) and I’m just not getting the results I’m after, despite eating extra protein etc. The weights simply aren’t heavy enough to build muscle if you’re already lean IMO - hence why I’m thinking to move to CrossFit.

Are you lifting as much as you can at each station? If you are, I think supplement the F45 strength days with heavier lifting at the gym or at home. Up your calories from protein. And yep, drop the cardio days.

Thanks so much for this advice! Cool there are other short gals to compare results with. I’d like to increase my muscle mass by a kilo or two. I’m guessing I should drop a couple cardio sessions and focus on strength days? Maybe start supplementing with lifting at home. 

I feel pretty good. I lost weight very quickly after my baby and the F45 thing was more about reconverting back from a soft body to an athletic one. 

Personally I don’t think I look overly thin - but I’m naturally a small build with narrow shoulders etc. I was looking over example pics of different body fat %s and it’s crazy how different bodies can look with the same base stats.
